The register says applicant is "Sartorius Weighing Technology GmbH", the document (certificate itself, as the legal instrument) says "Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co KG".

Is this spelling drift or legal-suffix drift? No — these are genuinely different legal entity names. Sartorius Weighing Technology GmbH and Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG are actually different legal entities within the Sartorius group (historically, Sartorius Weighing Technology GmbH was renamed/restructured; Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG is the current operating entity). But per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

The names differ beyond suffix drift — different legal form (GmbH vs GmbH & Co KG) and different middle names. So verdict: different-entity, best_value: "Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co KG".
